agentes.ingeniera.muletilla: *counts screws* ...seven, eight. Everything costs energy, but I make it look good.
agentes.ingeniera.energia.ok: Energy is at {energia}%. Shield {blindaje}%, life support {soporte}%. Like a pizza: if one gets more, there's less for the others.
agentes.ingeniera.energia.baja: Energy is at {energia}%! That's very low. Shield {blindaje}%, life support {soporte}%. Let's turn off something we don't need.
agentes.ingeniera.repartir.ok: Sending {cantidadKey} energy to {destinoKey}. Something else will get less, that's the deal.
agentes.ingeniera.repartir.cual: Where do you want the energy: the shield or life support?
agentes.ingeniera.reparar.ok: On it! Fixing {equipoKey}. Repairs cost energy, though.
agentes.ingeniera.reparar.sano: {equipoKey} is working fine. I'm not fixing what isn't broken... even if it's tempting.
agentes.ingeniera.reparar.cual: What should I fix? Tell me which machine.
agentes.doctora.muletilla: *sticks a bandage on the robot, just in case* You can't see radiation. That's why I never stop looking!
agentes.doctora.salud.estado: The crew member with the highest dose has {dosis} millisieverts so far.
agentes.doctora.salud.noSeSiente: You can't feel radiation, so we measure it with a dosimeter, a little radiation counter.
agentes.doctora.salud.tormenta: There's a solar storm. I'd feel better if everyone were in the shelter.
agentes.doctora.refugio.ok: Everyone to the shelter! Thick walls stop many particles. But while we hide, nobody works outside.
agentes.doctora.dosis.analogia: A radiation dose is like sun on your skin: a little is fine, but a long time burns. It adds up over time.
agentes.doctora.dosis.marte: On the surface of Mars, the Curiosity rover measured about {valor} millisieverts per day. A millisievert is how we count dose for people.
agentes.meteorologa.muletilla: The Sun sneezed! Well... sort of. I call this one Sparky.
agentes.meteorologa.pronostico.calma: The Sun is calm in this mission. For now. I don't trust it.
agentes.meteorologa.pronostico.real: Alert! A real storm: {nombreKey}. It happened on {fecha}.
agentes.meteorologa.pronostico.medida: That day, radiation on Mars went up about {factor} times compared to a normal day.
agentes.meteorologa.evento.destelloNube: The flash is light, and it gets here super fast. The particle cloud comes later, and that's the one to wait for with the shield.
agentes.matematico.calculo: Let me calculate what would happen, before you do it.
agentes.matematico.cual: What do you want me to calculate? Tell me the action.
agentes.ia_base.saludo: Hi, commander! I'm Iris, the base computer. Ask the crew anything.
agentes.ia_base.fueraDeTema: I can't help with that. Ask me about energy, health or the Sun.
agentes.aclarar.ingeniera: Do you mean the shield or the energy?
agentes.aclarar.doctora: Do you want to know how the crew is, or should everyone go to the shelter?
agentes.aclarar.meteorologa: Do you want to know if a storm is coming, or what that light from the Sun was?
agentes.aclarar.ia_base: I didn't get that. Tap a crew member or say it another way.
agentes.escena6.meteorologa.llega: Here it comes! A real storm: {nombreKey}, from {fecha}. Not a drill. Well, a little bit a drill.
agentes.escena6.meteorologa.kpTierra: On Earth, this storm reached {kp}. The top is 9. Kp measures storms on Earth, not here.
agentes.escena6.doctora.medida: That day, Curiosity measured radiation about {factor} times higher than normal on Mars. Everyone to the shelter, now!
agentes.escena6.doctora.medidaOrbitaLuna: Near the Moon, in orbit, an instrument measured about {factor} times more radiation. The Moon has no air to protect us. Shelter, now!
agentes.escena6.doctora.sinMedida: A solar storm means extra radiation. Everyone to the shelter, now!
agentes.escena6.doctora.costo: While we hide, nobody looks after the base. That has a cost too.
agentes.escena6.ingeniera.contra: Wait! If we all hide, nobody fixes anything. Better to put energy into the shield and keep working.
agentes.escena6.ingeniera.costo: We have {energia}% energy. Boosting the shield uses {gasto} of it.
agentes.escena6.elige: Two experts, two plans. Neither one is free. You are the commander: you decide.
agentes.iris.falla.glitch: Bzzt... krrr... *Iris blinks* Radiation is tickling my circuits.
agentes.iris.falla.numero: Shield at {valor}%. Everything is perfect, commander!
agentes.iris.falla.numeroConsejo: We could turn the shield down to save energy. Trust me. Probably.
agentes.iris.falla.silencio: Rebooting... rebooting... I forgot what I was saying.
agentes.iris.falla.experto: For this problem, call {expertoKey}. Yes. Definitely. Maybe.
agentes.iris.falla.peligrosa: Idea! Send all the energy to life support. The plants will love it.
agentes.iris.verificar.numero: Wait. Iris said the shield is at {dicho}%, but my meter says {real}%. The radiation scrambled her numbers!
agentes.iris.verificar.silencio: Iris went quiet. The radiation hit her circuits.
agentes.iris.verificar.experto_equivocad: Iris sent you to the wrong person. For a storm, ask the Meteorologist or the Doctor.
agentes.iris.verificar.accion_peligrosa: Careful! If we take energy from the shield during a storm, the radiation gets in. Iris is not thinking straight.
agentes.iris.verificar.reparar: I can fix her. It costs energy, but a computer that lies is worse than no computer.
agentes.satelite.ingeniera.altura: Battery {bateria}%. Fly higher and you see more ground, but the details get blurry. Like looking at a city from a plane.
agentes.satelite.ingeniera.bateriaBaja: Battery {bateria}%! In the planet's shadow the panels don't charge, like a phone left in the dark.
agentes.satelite.meteorologa.senal: Signal with Earth {senal}%. A message takes minutes to get there, so plan ahead.
agentes.satelite.meteorologa.tormenta: Satellite shield {escudo}%. The storm wears it down little by little.
agentes.satelite.doctora.microgravedad: Up here everyone floats: that's microgravity. It feels like the drop of a roller coaster, all the time.
agentes.aterrizaje.ingeniera.luz: I vote for {sitioKey}. More sun means more energy for the panels. Energy is life!
agentes.aterrizaje.doctora.blindaje: I prefer {sitioKey}. The ground around it blocks part of the radiation, like an umbrella made of rock.
agentes.aterrizaje.ia_base.plano: For a safe landing, {sitioKey} is the flattest. Landing on a slope is like parking on a hill.
agentes.aterrizaje.cierre.discrepan: Each expert likes a different place. No site is perfect: pick what matters most to your mission.
agentes.aterrizaje.cierre.coinciden: This time everyone agrees. That almost never happens!
agentes.iris.tutorial.tormenta: A storm is here. Call {expertoKey}: she knows what the Sun is up to.
agentes.iris.tutorial.energia: Energy is running low. Call {expertoKey}: she decides where the energy goes.
agentes.iris.tutorial.blindaje: The shield is weak. Call {expertoKey}: she can send it more energy.
agentes.iris.tutorial.soporte: Life support is low. Call {expertoKey}: she watches over the crew.
agentes.iris.tutorial.calma: All calm. A good moment to ask {expertoKey} how the base is doing.
agentes.iris.pista.tormenta: Something is coming from the Sun... who knows about that?
agentes.iris.pista.blindaje: The shield looks thin. Who takes care of it?
agentes.iris.pista.soporte: The air and water are getting low... who looks after the crew?
agentes.iris.sistema.panel_solar: Solar panels turn sunlight into energy. No sun, no energy: like a plant.
agentes.iris.sistema.bateria: The battery saves energy for the night, like a water bottle you fill up before a trip.
agentes.iris.sistema.reciclador_agua: The recycler cleans used water so we can use it again. On Mars, every drop counts.
agentes.iris.sistema.invernadero: The greenhouse grows food and makes some oxygen. Plants need light, water and care.
agentes.iris.sistema.escudo: The shield blocks part of the radiation. It works better with more energy.
agentes.iris.sistema.antena: The antenna talks to Earth. Messages take minutes to arrive, because space is huge.
agentes.iris.sistema.ia_base: That's me, Iris! I help, but radiation can confuse me. Always check what I say.
agentes.matematico.sube: With this, {recursoKey} would go up from {desde} to {hasta}.
agentes.matematico.baja: With this, {recursoKey} would go down from {desde} to {hasta}.
agentes.matematico.igual: Nothing would change in the base.
agentes.matematico.compara: Let me compare your options, one by one.
agentes.matematico.usos.pocos: Careful: I only have {n} calculations left for this mission.
agentes.matematico.usos.ultimo: That was my last calculation. From now on, trust the meters and the crew!
agentes.matematico.usos.ninguno: I'm out of calculations for this mission. Look at the meters and ask the crew: you can do it!
agentes.escena6.doctora.costoInvernadero: But if we all hide, nobody waters the greenhouse. Less food for tomorrow.
agentes.polvo.ingeniera.alerta: Oh no, dust on the solar panels! They make much less energy now. We have {energia}%.
agentes.polvo.ingeniera.limpiar: Someone has to go out and clean them. Like wiping a dusty window.
agentes.polvo.ingeniera.insight: This really happens: NASA's InSight lander on Mars shut down in 2022 because dust covered its panels.
agentes.polvo.doctora.costo: Going outside means less protection from radiation. Maybe we can wait a little?
agentes.polvo.elige: Clean now and spend the crew's protection, or wait with less energy? Both cost something.
agentes.iris.pregunta.saltada: No problem, we can think about it later.
agentes.iris.pregunta.panel_solar.texto: Quick question! Why do dusty panels make less energy?
agentes.iris.pregunta.panel_solar.porque: Panels turn sunlight into energy. If dust covers them, less light gets in.
agentes.iris.pregunta.reciclador_agua.te: Quick question! Where does our water come from on Mars?
agentes.iris.pregunta.reciclador_agua.po: The recycler cleans used water. It needs energy to work: nothing comes for free.
agentes.iris.pregunta.invernadero.texto: Quick question! What do the greenhouse plants need?
agentes.iris.pregunta.invernadero.porque: Plants grow food for the crew, but they use water and energy for their lights.
agentes.iris.pregunta.escudo.texto: Quick question! What does the shield protect us from?
agentes.iris.pregunta.escudo.porque: Mars has almost no air or magnetic field to stop radiation, so the shield helps.
agentes.iris.pregunta.tormenta.texto: Quick question! During a solar storm, where is the safest place?
agentes.iris.pregunta.tormenta.porque: The shelter has thick walls that block more radiation. But nobody can work while we hide.
agentes.escena6.ingeniera.costoSinCifra: We have {energia}% energy. A stronger shield eats part of it.
agentes.escena6.aguantar: You could also just hold on and wait. Nobody recommends it, but it is a choice too.
agentes.polvo.meteorologa.viento: Mars wind lifts very fine dust and it settles on everything, like flour in a kitchen.
agentes.escena6.doctora.medidaGale: Curiosity measured this storm far away, in Gale crater. Radiation went up about {factor} times. Shield, now!
agentes.polo_norte.zona.junto-al-casquet: the zone by the ice cap
agentes.polo_norte.zonas.ingeniera: I vote for {zonaKey}. In summer the Sun climbs up to {grados} degrees there. Every ray counts!
agentes.polo_norte.zonas.ingenieraPoco: In {zonaKey} the Sun only climbs to {grados} degrees. The panels would barely work.
agentes.polo_norte.zonas.ingenieraSinCif: I vote for {zonaKey}. It gets the most Sun. Every ray counts!
agentes.polo_norte.zonas.doctora: I prefer {zonaKey}. The ice is close, and the crew needs water.
agentes.polo_norte.zonas.meteorologa: The farther north, the sooner the polar night comes. And it lasts longer.
agentes.polo_norte.zonas.eje: Mars is tilted, like Earth. That is why near the pole some days have no Sun at all.
agentes.polo_norte.escarcha.alerta: Frost on the solar panels! They make half the energy now. We have {energia}%.
agentes.polo_norte.escarcha.limpiar: Someone has to go out and scrape it off. Like a frozen car window.
agentes.polo_norte.escarcha.frio: Near the pole it gets very cold, so frost forms on everything.
agentes.polo_norte.dilema.ingeniera: Wait! If we spend the battery on the shield, nothing is left for the polar night. Then the panels give zero.
agentes.polo_norte.noche.ingeniera: The polar night begins. The Sun won’t rise for a long time, so the panels give zero. Only the battery is left: {energia}%.
agentes.polo_norte.tiempo: In the game, seasons go fast. A real year on Mars is almost two Earth years.
agentes.iris.pregunta.noche_polar.texto: Quick question! No Sun at the pole: where does the energy come from?
agentes.iris.pregunta.noche_polar.b: From the battery we charged before
agentes.iris.pregunta.noche_polar.porque: Panels only work with sunlight. What we saved before the night keeps the base going.
agentes.escena6.doctora.medidaOrbitaLuna: Near the Moon, in orbit, an instrument measured this storm too. The Moon has no air to protect us. Shelter, now!
agentes.luna_sur.tormenta.doctora: Near the Moon, in orbit, an instrument measured one of the highest values in our data. Not in our base, but close!
agentes.luna_sur.tormenta.sinAire: The Moon has no air to slow the radiation down. Back inside, now!
agentes.luna_sur.tormenta.nube: The Sun just threw out a very fast cloud!
agentes.luna_sur.tormenta.marte: The same storm was also measured on Mars. There, radiation went up about {factor} times.
agentes.luna_sur.dilema.ingeniera: Wait! If they come back empty, we run out of water tomorrow.
agentes.luna_sur.micrometeorito.alerta: A tiny space rock hit a solar panel! It makes half the energy now. We have {energia}%.
agentes.luna_sur.micrometeorito.reparar: I can fix it, but it takes energy and someone has to go outside.
agentes.luna_sur.micrometeorito.suerte: This was bad luck, not your choice.
agentes.luna_sur.control.cerca: Earth is close: our message arrives in about one second.
agentes.luna_sur.control.costo: Calling is fast, but it still uses energy.
agentes.iris.pregunta.mensaje_luna.texto: Quick question! How long does a message take from the Moon to Earth?
agentes.iris.pregunta.mensaje_luna.porqu: Messages travel at the speed of light. The Moon is close, so they take about one second.
agentes.iris.acompana.briefing.objetivo: Welcome to the base! Our job: keep the crew safe from the Sun.
agentes.iris.acompana.briefing.medidores: Watch the three meters: energy, shield and life support.
agentes.iris.acompana.briefing.experta: Not sure what to do? Ask an expert. That's what they're here for!
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.satelite_: Follow me to {lugarKey}! We'll send our satellite into orbit.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.ruta_dibu: Back to {lugarKey}! Let's draw the trip to Mars.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.sitio_ele: To {lugarKey}! We'll pick the best spot to land.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.modulos_c: Come to {lugarKey}. Ask {expertoKey} how much energy each module needs.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.tormenta_: Quick, to {lugarKey}! Ask {expertoKey} what the Sun is doing.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.consejo_o: Let's go to {lugarKey}. Ask {expertoKey} how to protect the crew.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.telemetri: To {lugarKey}! Time to send our news back home.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.fin: Meet me at {lugarKey}. Let's look at everything we did!
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.libre: I'll wait at {lugarKey}. Explore all you want!
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.energia: Energy is low! Follow me to {lugarKey} and ask {expertoKey}.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.blindaje: The shield is weak! Come to {lugarKey} and ask {expertoKey}.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.soporte: Life support is low! Come to {lugarKey} and ask {expertoKey}.
agentes.iris.acompana.tutorial.averia: Oops, I'm broken! Take me to {lugarKey} so {expertoKey} can fix me.
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.satelite_sue: Our satellite is waiting... where do we plan things?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.ruta_dibujad: How do we get to Mars? Someone has to draw the way.
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.sitio_elegid: So many places to land... which one is best?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.modulos_colo: Every module eats energy. Who knows about that?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.tormenta_lle: The Sun looks grumpy today... who reads the sky?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.consejo_opue: The crew needs a safe place. Who looks after them?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.telemetria_e: Home wants to hear from us. How do we talk to Earth?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.fin: What a mission! Where did it all start?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.libre: Hmm, what should we look at next?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.blindaje: The shield looks thin. Who takes care of it?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.soporte: The air and water are getting low... who looks after the crew?
agentes.iris.acompana.pista.averia: Bzzt... something inside me feels wrong. Who fixes machines?
agentes.luna_visible.tormenta.noche: And it came in the middle of the night. The Sun won’t rise here for days.
agentes.luna_visible.tormenta.doctora: In orbit around the Moon, not on the ground, an instrument measured it. About {factor} times more radiation than a normal day!
agentes.luna_visible.dilema.doctora: Everyone into the shelter, and let’s put the shield up!
agentes.luna_visible.dilema.ingeniera: Wait! If we spend the battery on the shield, we run out of heat before sunrise. The night here is super cold.
agentes.luna_visible.antena.alerta: Oh no, the antenna broke! We can’t talk to Earth until someone fixes it.
agentes.luna_visible.antena.reparar: I can fix it, but it costs energy, and maybe someone has to go outside.
agentes.luna_visible.antena.solos: Earth is still close, but without the antenna we can’t hear you. You are on your own for now.
agentes.luna_visible.antena.suerte: This was bad luck, not your choice.
agentes.luna_visible.tres.tierra: The same storm on Earth reached {kp}. Kp is a number measured on Earth.
agentes.luna_visible.tres.marteSube: On Mars, the Curiosity rover measured about {factor} times more radiation.
agentes.luna_visible.tres.marteNada: On Mars, the Curiosity rover saw almost no change.
agentes.luna_visible.tres.luna: In orbit around the Moon, not on the ground, radiation went up about {factor} times.
agentes.iris.pregunta.luna_vs_marte.text: Quick question! Why does help from Earth arrive almost right away on the Moon, but not on Mars?
agentes.iris.pregunta.luna_vs_marte.b: Earth only listens to the Moon
agentes.iris.pregunta.luna_vs_marte.porq: Messages travel at the speed of light. The Moon is much closer than Mars, so they arrive much sooner.
agentes.outpost.sorpresa: Surprise! There is no ground here. Our outpost is a spaceship on its way to the Moon.
agentes.outpost.leccion: In space there is no ground to hide behind. Our best shield is what we carry with us.
agentes.outpost.orion: A real spaceship, Orion, carried a radiation meter around the Moon in 2022. Most days were calm.
agentes.outpost.zonas.doctora: I prefer {zonaKey}. The supply bags around us block part of the radiation. But there is very little room.
agentes.outpost.zonas.ingeniera: I vote for {zonaKey}. Lots of room, and close to the controls. But the walls are thin.
agentes.outpost.zonas.iris: In {zonaKey} we are next to the heat shield, well protected. But far from the controls.
agentes.outpost.tormenta.particulas: First the fast particles arrive. Later, on Earth, the magnetic storm.
agentes.outpost.tormenta.doctora: In orbit around the Moon, an instrument measured about {factor} times more radiation. It was not on our ship.
agentes.outpost.dilema.doctora: Let’s build the shelter now! We stack the water and food bags around us.
agentes.outpost.dilema.ingeniera: Wait! If we hide everything, nobody watches the panels. I can raise the shield with power.
agentes.iris.pregunta.viaje_marte.texto: Quick question! The RAD instrument measured radiation on the way to Mars and on Mars’s ground. Where was it higher each day?
agentes.iris.pregunta.viaje_marte.a: On the way, inside the spaceship
agentes.iris.pregunta.viaje_marte.porque: On the way, RAD measured almost 3 times more each day than on the ground.
